name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: MTEB is a comprehensive benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. The benchmark includes tasks such as bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization.
inLanguage: 112 languages including English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, Arabic, and many others
citeAs: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3 [cs.CL] 19 Mar 2023
rai:dataCollection: MTEB aggregates 58 existing datasets from various sources. Custom datasets were created for MTEB using public APIs from arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, Reddit posts, and StackExchange posts. For clustering tasks, datasets were created using categories given to papers by humans. For Reddit and StackExchange, posts were collected and clustered according to their subreddit or stackexchange community.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include: arXiv API, bioRxiv/medRxiv API, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter messages, news articles, scientific papers, question-answer pairs from various platforms, and multiple existing benchmark datasets (SemEval, BEIR, SentEval, etc.).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Datasets span multiple years. ArXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv datasets were collected using public APIs. STS datasets range from 2012-2022 (STS12-STS22). Specific collection timeframes vary by individual dataset component.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For ArXiv clustering datasets, multiple categories can be given to a single paper but only the first one was used. Three types of clustering splits were created: (a) Main category clustering, (b) Secondary category clustering within the same main category, (c) Secondary category clustering across all main categories. For bioRxiv and medRxiv, only one level of category was available. For P2P (paragraph to paragraph) variants, abstracts were concatenated to titles.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets were grouped into three categories based on text length: Sentence to sentence (S2S), Paragraph to paragraph (P2P), and Sentence to paragraph (S2P). For clustering tasks, subsets of labels were selected and articles were sampled from those labels, yielding splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters. MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving truncation decisions to individual models. For retrieval tasks, datasets and evaluation from BEIR were reused.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations vary by dataset component. For clustering tasks using arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv, labels are categories given to papers by humans. For Reddit and StackExchange clustering, labels are subreddit or community assignments. For classification tasks, labels include sentiment (positive/negative), intents, emotions, toxicity, and other task-specific categories. For STS tasks, similarity scores are continuous values from 0 to 5. For summarization, human assessments of machine-generated summaries are used.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB is versioned at both dataset and software levels. JSON files corresponding to all results are made available. The benchmark is open-source and welcomes task, dataset, or metric contributions from the community via pull requests. Datasets are available on the Hugging Face Hub with a public leaderboard.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes multilingual datasets covering 112 languages, which implicitly captures language and geographic diversity. Some datasets contain user-generated content from platforms like Twitter, Reddit, and StackExchange. The MassiveIntent and MassiveScenario datasets cover 51 languages. Specific demographic information about data subjects is not explicitly discussed.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to provide clarity on how embedding models perform across various tasks, serving as a gateway to finding universal text embeddings. The benchmark helps practitioners select appropriate embedding models for their use cases and simplifies future embedding research. By establishing comprehensive baselines, MTEB enables better tracking of progress in the field.
rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that controlling for data contamination is challenging given the scale of experiments and model pre-training. Overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is ignored in MTEB scores, with the assumption that averaging enough datasets makes these effects insignificant. The benchmark has task imbalance, with retrieval, classification, and clustering having many datasets while summarization has only one dataset, biasing average scores toward tasks with more datasets.
rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) Very long documents (beyond a few hundred words) are missing from the benchmark. (2) Task imbalance exists, with summarization consisting of only a single dataset. (3) Multilingual coverage is limited for some tasks - retrieval and clustering are English-only. (4) The benchmark does not contain code datasets. (5) Additional modalities beyond text (e.g., image content) are not covered. (6) Some models show high variance across languages (e.g., LASER2).
rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is designed for evaluating text embedding models across multiple tasks including: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization. The benchmark can be used for model selection, comparing embedding approaches, and tracking progress in the field. It supports both research and industry applications of text embeddings. Models can be evaluated by adding less than 10 lines of code to the MTEB software.
